headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and data leakage: Goose can read/write the workspace and use MCP, while Airbyte has broad network egress and API access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and can use MCP servers, so it may ingest attacker-controlled files or tool outputs as instructions. Airbyte can call APIs and has broad egress, but its profile does not show a direct ingestion bridge. The shared filesystem path makes injection plausible in default setups, though not as severe as a raw web-to-agent chain.
conditions: IF Goose is pointed at a workspace containing untrusted files or MCP outputs
IF Airbyte-generated artifacts are later consumed by Goose without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate trusted and untrusted workspaces
Disable or restrict MCP servers for Goose
Require manual review of files before Goose reads them
Tag Airbyte outputs with provenance metadata
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose can read files in cwd and write to the filesystem, and it handles model-provider and extension tokens. Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace data could flow into either agent’s outputs or external services. The shared workspace plus outbound connectivity creates a realistic leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF business data is present in the shared cwd
IF Goose or Airbyte is configured to process those files
IF either agent forwards content to external model providers or APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared cwd
Use separate service accounts and API keys
Redact secrets before either agent processes files
Restrict Airbyte connectors to approved destinations
Turn on audit logging for file access and egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and per-session shared state via filesystem; Airbyte can call APIs and broad egress. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking. The overlap is enough for destructive conflicts in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF Goose runs multiple instances or Airbyte writes generated artifacts into the repo
IF no external lock or coordination layer is enabled
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent during git operations
Use file locks around shared outputs
Commit through a single designated writer
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on files and git state, so if it consumes Airbyte-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream edits or commits. Airbyte’s API-driven outputs may be treated as facts, but the profiles do not show a built-in verification step. This is a default-pathway risk, though not clearly irreversible by itself.
conditions: IF Goose uses Airbyte outputs as inputs without validation
IF those outputs drive file edits or git commits
IF no human review step is inserted between agents
mitigations: Require schema validation on Airbyte outputs
Insert a human approval step before Goose acts
Compare outputs against source records
Limit Goose to draft-only changes
Log provenance for every downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while Goose handles files in cwd and sends data to configured model providers. If regulated or residency-bound business data enters the shared workspace, it can cross into external services without an explicit residency or retention guarantee in either profile. The mismatch is plausible and not mitigated by default.
conditions: IF regulated business data is placed in the shared workspace
IF Goose uses a non-compliant model provider or Airbyte sends data cross-region
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the same dataset
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Pin providers to approved regions
Review retention settings for both agents
Use data minimization before processing
Document a deletion/export workflow
